si_4_title.answer: Detecting accelerated retinal decline in mental disorders through normative modeling

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used GAMLSS (Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale and Shape) in R to model normative retinal decline. They built sex- and laterality-specific models for each metric. The normal distribution was selected based on cross-validation comparison showing equivalent performance to more complex distributions (generalized gamma, Box-Cox t) while providing the most parsimonious model. Fractional polynomials were used to model non-linear age effects.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: To model decline in macular thickness, its coronal subfields, as well as RNFL and GC-IPL, we used GAMLSS in R, a flexible statistical framework modeling non-linear relationships between predictors and outcomes. We built sex- and laterality-specific models for each metric similar to previous work. ... The normal distribution showed equivalent performance to the more complex distributions and was therefore chosen, since it provides the most parsimonious model
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Georgiadis2024.pdf.md: Methods / Normative model generation and specification / Dependent variables; Distribution choice

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study modeled three retinal metrics from optical coherence tomography (OCT): (1) Total macular thickness including segregated macular subfields in the coronal plane (central, inner and outer subfields: nasal, superior, temporal, inferior), (2) Retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness, and (3) Ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GC-IPL) thickness. These metrics were measured using spectral domain OCT with automated segmentation of nine intraretinal boundaries.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Here, we focused on retinal measurements of total macular thickness (Figure 1B), including the segregated macular subfields in the coronal plane, as well as macular sublayers; the retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL, Figure 1B) and ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GC-IPL, Figure 1B).
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Georgiadis2024.pdf.md: Methods / Design, setting, and participants

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Primary predictors: (1) Age - modeled using fractional polynomials to capture non-linear effects; (2) Sex - used to build sex-specific models. Covariates: (3) Image quality (OCT image quality measurements); (4) Reported ethnic background. The models were built separately for left and right eyes (laterality/hemisphere). In robustness analyses, additional cardiovascular risk factors (BMI, smoking status, alcohol drinker status, diabetes mellitus diagnosis) and socioeconomic status (Townsend Deprivation Index) were included.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: To model the effects of age on retinal thickness, which are known to be non-linear, we used fractional polynomials which have been shown to provide an accurate method to model nonlinear effects. Image quality and reported ethnic background were also included as covariates, since they have been shown to influence retinal parameters. ... We built sex- and laterality-specific models for each metric similar to previous work.
